name: Prometheus
summary: A monitoring system that stores labeled time series, evaluates PromQL expressions, and collects samples through scrape and rule-evaluation workflows.

features.name: Labeled time-series data model
features.description: Prometheus identifies a time series by a metric name and set of labels, with samples carrying timestamped values. Labels therefore form part of series identity and query selection.
benefits: Keeps metric identity explicit in storage and query APIs
costs: High label cardinality expands series and index state
Changing labels creates distinct series rather than updating one identity

features.name: PromQL expression evaluation
features.description: Prometheus evaluates PromQL expressions over instant and range vectors, applying selectors, operators, functions, and aggregations to produce scalar, string, or vector results.
benefits: Combines selection, transformation, and aggregation in one query language
Makes time and label dimensions first-class query inputs
costs: Query cost depends on range, cardinality, and expression shape
Query semantics must account for missing samples and staleness

features.name: Scrape and rule-evaluation workflows
features.description: Prometheus periodically scrapes configured targets and can evaluate recording and alerting rules, writing resulting samples and alert state back into the monitoring workflow.
benefits: Uses a pull-based collection boundary with explicit target discovery
Turns recurring queries into stored series or alert decisions
costs: Availability and freshness depend on scrape scheduling and target reachability
Rule evaluation adds recurring query and storage load

mathematical_views.question: How do label sets and timestamps define a relation from metric identity to ordered samples?
assumptions: A label set identifies one logical series at a time
Samples are interpreted with Prometheus timestamp and staleness rules
Storage encoding and compaction are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: How do selectors, range vectors, functions, operators, and aggregations transform labeled samples over time?
assumptions: PromQL evaluation rules define operator domains and result types
The evaluation timestamp is fixed for one query step

mathematical_views.question: How does a scheduled scrape and rule loop convert target observations into stored series and alert state?
assumptions: Targets expose compatible metrics when reachable
Scheduling and timeout behavior are explicit inputs
The view does not claim that every scrape succeeds

costs: Cardinality and label hygiene become central resource constraints
Complex queries can consume substantial CPU and memory

benefits: Simple recurring pull and evaluation model
costs: Freshness depends on scheduling, target health, and rule load
